findings.evidence: Lines 139–148 provide `commonRefinement_fst` and `commonRefinement_snd`; the implementation at lines 133–135 therefore need not be unfoldable.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` and add any further projection/cover lemmas consumers need.
findings.issue: `commonRefinement` is marked `@[expose]` even though its projections already have public simp lemmas, unnecessarily making downstream proofs depend on its body.

findings.evidence: The only new API lemmas are `commonRefinement_fst`, `commonRefinement_snd`, and `commonRefinement_I` at lines 139–155, all parameterized by a supplied `r`; no lemma mentions `(t.commonRefinementOf s)`, and no `commonRefinement_X` lemma exists.
findings.fix: Add simp projection lemmas for `commonRefinementOf` and characteristic lemmas exposing the shared index and covering family for both constructions, with the necessary transports made explicit.
findings.issue: Opaque `commonRefinementOf` has no projection, index, or covering-object lemmas, so consumers cannot characterize its atlases or use the promised common cover without unfolding an unavailable body; even supplied `commonRefinement` only states equality of `I`, not its `X` families.

summary: The new refinement operations expose an implementation body while leaving the canonical construction and shared-cover property without a usable characteristic API.
